questions.q: In the lab scenario, what two reports does the Service Desk Manager's request split into?
options: A Pivot Table of changes by state, and a List of all incidents ever created
A Pie chart of open incidents by priority, and a Bar chart of open incidents by assignment group
A single Time Series report with no filter
A PA indicator with no underlying report at all
questions.explain: "How bad is the backlog" maps to a Pie chart grouped by Priority; "which team is carrying it" maps to a Bar chart grouped by Assignment group.

questions.q: What do the two reports in the lab have in common?
options: Nothing — they run against completely different tables
The same table and the same Active-is-true filter, differing only in group-by field and chart type
They are both Pivot Tables
Neither one uses a filter condition
questions.explain: Both run on the incident table filtered to Active is true; only the group-by field (Priority vs. Assignment group) and chart type (Pie vs. Bar) differ.

questions.q: What must be true before you can open the Dashboard application and start assembling the manager's dashboard?
options: A collector job must have run at least once
Both reports must already exist, built and saved in Report Designer
The dashboard must already have a role restriction applied
Performance Analytics must be licensed, even though this lab uses no PA widgets
questions.explain: The lab follows report-first, dashboard-second: both reports are built and named in Report Designer before either is placed on a dashboard canvas.

questions.q: Why does the lab set a refresh interval on the finished dashboard?
options: Refresh interval is required before any widget can be added at all
Because the dashboard is meant to stay open on a screen through the day, and should stay current without manual reloads
To change which role can see the dashboard
Refresh interval controls the chart type, not the data
questions.explain: For a dashboard meant to sit open as a running view, a refresh interval keeps its widgets' counts current automatically.

questions.q: At what point in the lab does the Service Desk Manager role restriction get applied, and why does that timing matter?
options: Before either report is built, because visibility has to exist before data does
It never gets applied in this lab — the dashboard is left open to everyone
As the final step, after the dashboard is assembled, set deliberately rather than as an afterthought — so the dashboard reaches exactly its intended audience
Only inside Performance Analytics, never inside the Dashboard application
questions.explain: The lab applies the restriction as a deliberate final step, matching Lesson 30's point that visibility is a core design decision, not something to fix later.
